author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell reacts to talk of conscription, war with Russia, and proposals to silence pro-Russian voices before turning to what he sees as a deeper problem: bureaucracy itself.

Drawing on C.S. Lewis, Russell argues that bureaucracy can reduce people to purely rational and transactional beings, stripping away spirit, humor, joy, sexuality and personal power. His broader point is that systems become easier to control when people forget the parts of themselves that make them fully human.

description:

author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell reacts to comments about Britain, conscription, and pro-Russian voices before widening the conversation into what he sees as a recurring pattern: institutions offering safety, convenience, or support while asking for greater compliance in return.

He connects that concern to vaccines, implanted chips, universal basic income, central digital currency, and digital ID, arguing that systems sold as convenient could also become tools of control if access can be switched on or off depending on obedience. These are Russell’s arguments and hypotheticals in the clip, rather than established conclusions about how these technologies or policies necessarily work.
